evidence.snippet: Patients are homozygous for a splice-site mutation in ABCC9 (c.1320 + 1 G > A), which encodes the sulfonylurea receptor 2 (SUR2) subunit of KATP channels.
evidence.explanation: Identifies the founding biallelic ABCC9 lesion.

evidence.snippet: All variants are predicted to result in severe truncations or in-frame deletions within SUR2, leading to the generation of non-functional SUR2-dependent KATP channels.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the truncating/in-frame-deletion allele class across seven further families.

evidence.snippet: All variants are predicted to lead to nonsense mediated decay of ABCC9 transcripts and/or drastic truncation of SUR2.
evidence.explanation: Confirms nonsense-mediated decay and truncation as the mechanism of allele inactivation in the most recent cohort.

evidence.snippet: The phenotype differs from Cantú syndrome, which is caused by gain-of-function ABCC9 mutations, reflecting the opposing consequences of KATP loss- versus gain-of-function.
evidence.explanation: Anchors the direction of effect that separates AIMS from the other ABCC9 disease, Cantu syndrome.

steps/1.description: Biallelic loss-of-function variants in ABCC9 - splice-site alleles causing in-frame exon skipping, and nonsense or frameshift alleles causing nonsense-mediated decay or drastic truncation - abolish production of functional SUR2 protein. This is the root lesion of AIMS and is the opposite direction of effect to the gain-of-function ABCC9 variants that cause Cantu syndrome.

evidence.snippet: We term this channelopathy resulting from loss-of-function of SUR2-containing KATP channels ABCC9-related Intellectual disability Myopathy Syndrome (AIMS).
evidence.explanation: Names the loss of SUR2-containing KATP channel function as the defining lesion of the syndrome.

evidence.snippet: KATP channels are found throughout the cardiovascular system and skeletal muscle and couple cellular metabolism to excitability.
evidence.explanation: States the tissue distribution and the metabolism-to-excitability coupling role that is lost when SUR2 is absent.

steps/2.description: SUR2 is the regulatory subunit that confers ATP/ADP sensitivity and trafficking competence on Kir6.x pore subunits in skeletal muscle, cardiac muscle and vascular smooth muscle. Without functional SUR2, the SUR2-containing KATP channels of those tissues are absent or non-conducting, so cellular metabolic state can no longer be translated into membrane potassium conductance.

evidence.snippet: In skeletal muscle, K ATP channels are typically closed at rest but open in response to metabolic stress or fatigue
evidence.explanation: States the normal metabolic gating of the sarcolemmal channel that AIMS abolishes. Quoted with the space that the cached PDF text carries between "K" and "ATP".

steps/3.description: In healthy skeletal muscle the sarcolemmal KATP channel is closed at rest and opens as intracellular ATP falls during metabolic stress or fatigue. In AIMS muscle this metabolically gated conductance is absent.

evidence.snippet: Therefore, loss of KATP function might be expected to result in failure to recover from fatigue
evidence.explanation: The authors' explicit mechanistic prediction for what loss of the conductance does to a fatiguing fibre.

steps/4.description: Loss of the fatigue-activated potassium conductance removes the brake on sarcolemmal excitability during sustained activity, impairing recovery from fatigue and predisposing the fibre to contraction without stimulation.

evidence.snippet: In isolated muscle, SUR2 LoF results in abnormal generation of unstimulated forces, potentially explaining painful spasms in AIMS.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the unstimulated-force phenotype and its proposed clinical correlate.

steps/5.description: SUR2-null muscle generates force without stimulation under fatiguing conditions, the proposed cellular correlate of the painful spasms reported by patients. The downstream effector remains unresolved; CaV1.1-mediated calcium influx was tested directly and did not explain the myopathy.

evidence.snippet: KATP channels are found throughout the cardiovascular system and skeletal muscle and couple cellular metabolism to excitability.
evidence.explanation: Places the SUR2-containing channel in the cardiovascular system.

steps/6.description: SUR2-containing KATP channels in cardiomyocytes couple cellular metabolism to membrane excitability. Loss of functional SUR2 removes that metabolically responsive conductance.

evidence.snippet: Loss- or gain-of-function mutations in ATP-sensitive potassium channel (K-ATP)-encoding genes, KCNJ8 and ABCC9, cause human central nervous system disorders with unknown pathogenesis.
evidence.explanation: Frames the CNS arm of ABCC9 disease as the problem being addressed.

evidence.snippet: Our results demonstrate a role for KCNJ8/ABCC9-containing K-ATP channels in the differentiation of brain VSMC, which in turn is necessary for fine-tuning of cerebral blood flow.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the ABCC9-dependent brain vascular developmental role.

evidence.snippet: Consistent with defective VSMC development, Kcnj8 knockout mice showed deficiency in vasoconstrictive capacity and neuronal-evoked vasodilation leading to local hyperemia.
evidence.explanation: Marked PARTIAL because the in vivo neurovascular-coupling deficit was shown in a Kcnj8 (Kir6.1) knockout, the partner subunit, not in an Abcc9 knockout.

steps/7.description: KCNJ8/ABCC9-containing KATP channels are expressed on brain mural cell progenitors and are required cell-autonomously for arterial and arteriolar smooth muscle differentiation. Loss of channel function suppresses that differentiation and, in the corresponding knockout, degrades vasoconstrictive capacity and neuronally evoked vasodilation - the machinery that fine-tunes cerebral blood flow.

evidence.snippet: All patients report fatigability, present with generalized hypotonia, and muscle strength is below normal in all but one.
evidence.explanation: Documents the clinical myopathy across the index cohort.

evidence.snippet: S-CK, B-lactate, nerve conduction velocities, and electromyography, including repetitive nerve stimulation, are normal in all individuals
evidence.explanation: Shows the myopathy is not accompanied by the usual laboratory markers of muscle destruction, which is diagnostically important.

evidence.snippet: We found reduced exercise performance in mouse models of AIMS harboring premature stop codons in ABCC9.
evidence.explanation: The mouse model recapitulates the exercise-intolerance arm.

steps/8.description: A myopathy that is clinically prominent but histologically and electrophysiologically bland: patients have generalised hypotonia, reduced strength, fatigability and exercise-induced pain, with normal serum creatine kinase, normal nerve conduction and essentially normal electromyography.

evidence.snippet: All have cerebral white matter hyperintensities
evidence.explanation: Cerebral white matter hyperintensity in all six index patients.

evidence.snippet: Affected individuals show psychomotor delay and intellectual disability of variable severity, microcephaly, corpus callosum and white matter abnormalities, seizures, spasticity, short stature, muscle fatigability and weakness.
evidence.explanation: Confirms white matter and corpus callosum involvement in the expanded cohort.

evidence.snippet: These new cases further demonstrate the prominence of white matter abnormalities resembling periventricular leukomalacia or small vessel disease as a key hallmark of the disorder, alongside developmental delay, intellectual impairment, seizures, and fatigability.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the leukomalacia-like radiological pattern as a hallmark.

evidence.snippet: MR angiography is normal, with normal cerebral vasculature calibers.
evidence.explanation: The injury is not accompanied by a macrovascular abnormality, which is both consistent with a functional small-vessel mechanism and the point of contrast with the dilated tortuous vessels of Cantu syndrome.

steps/9.description: Cerebral white matter hyperintensities were present in every patient of the index cohort and white matter abnormalities, often with corpus callosum involvement, recur across the later cohorts. In the most recent series the pattern resembles periventricular leukomalacia or small vessel disease and is described as a key hallmark of the disorder. Lesions can progress over time.

evidence.snippet: Cardiac systolic dysfunction is found in the two oldest patients.
evidence.explanation: The human cardiac finding, with its age restriction.

evidence.snippet: AIMS individuals show fatigability, muscle spasms, and cardiac dysfunction.
evidence.explanation: Confirms cardiac dysfunction as part of the recognised human phenotype. Tagged OTHER rather than HUMAN_CLINICAL: this is the introductory framing sentence of a mouse-model paper restating the accepted clinical picture, not data that paper generated. The human cohort evidence is the PMID:31575858 item above.

steps/10.description: Reduced systolic function, documented in the two oldest patients of the index cohort and reproduced in SUR2-null mice and zebrafish. It is an age-related feature rather than a presenting one.

evidence.snippet: revealed mild-to-moderate intellectual disability in all affected individuals, and anxiety was also reported in several patients.
evidence.explanation: Formal neuropsychological testing confirmed intellectual disability in all six index patients.

evidence.snippet: These latest findings also highlight neonatal presentation of disease, deterioration following surgical procedures, and the potential for motor and cognitive decline, which should be monitored in older individuals.
evidence.explanation: Adds the later-life decline arm of the cognitive phenotype.

steps/11.description: Psychomotor delay followed by intellectual disability, mild in the index Norwegian families and of variable severity across the expanded cohorts. Motor and cognitive decline has now been documented in older individuals, including a sexagenarian presenting with signs of dementia.

steps/12.description: Lower-limb hyperreflexia and spasticity, appearing in the older patients of the index cohort and recorded as spasticity across the expanded cohort.

evidence.snippet: In vivo studies of abcc9 loss-of-function in zebrafish revealed an exacerbated motor response to pentylenetetrazole, a pro-convulsive drug, consistent with impaired neurodevelopment associated with an increased seizure susceptibility.

evidence.snippet: From age 15, she experienced episodes of tonic/tonic-clonic seizures, but epileptic activity was absent in repeated EEGs.
evidence.explanation: Marked PARTIAL because the clinical events in this index patient were not confirmed electrographically.

steps/13.description: Seizures occur in a proportion of AIMS patients, and abcc9 loss of function lowers the chemoconvulsant threshold in zebrafish. In the index cohort one patient had clinical tonic-clonic episodes without EEG correlate, so the epileptic phenotype is not uniform.

evidence.snippet: This mutation results in an in-frame deletion of exon 8, which results in non-functional KATP channels in recombinant assays.

evidence.snippet: Functional tests of recombinant channels confirm that disease-associated SUR2 truncations cause a complete loss-of-function.

edges/2.description: Absence of functional SUR2 protein prevents assembly of working SUR2-containing KATP channels.

evidence.snippet: Under fatiguing conditions, isometric tetanic contraction experiments on murine extensor digitorum longus (EDL) revealed delayed loss of stimulated forces, and significant development of unstimulated forces, in muscles lacking Kir6.2 or SUR2 subunits, whereas loss of the SUR1 subunit did not impact muscle functionality.
evidence.explanation: Subunit dissection shows that removing SUR2 (but not SUR1) abolishes the functionally relevant sarcolemmal KATP conductance of fast-twitch muscle.

evidence.snippet: ATP-sensitive potassium (KATP) channels are among the most expressed ion channels in skeletal muscle sarcolemma.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the sarcolemmal abundance of the channel that is lost.

edges/3.description: Fast-twitch skeletal muscle depends on noncanonical Kir6.2/SUR2 sarcolemmal KATP channels, so SUR2 loss removes essentially the whole sarcolemmal KATP conductance.

evidence.snippet: SUR2 loss-of-function causes fatigability and cardiac dysfunction in mice, and reduced activity, cardiac dysfunction and ventricular enlargement in zebrafish.
evidence.explanation: Two independent animal models lacking functional SUR2 develop cardiac dysfunction, linking absent cardiomyocyte SUR2 to the cardiac arm.

edges/4.description: SUR2A is the cardiac sulfonylurea receptor, so its loss removes cardiomyocyte KATP current.

evidence.snippet: We show that genetic/chemical inhibition or activation of KCNJ8/ABCC9-containing K-ATP channel function leads to brain-selective suppression or promotion of arterial/arteriolar vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) differentiation, respectively.
evidence.explanation: Inhibition of the ABCC9-containing channel suppresses brain VSMC differentiation, the direction of effect relevant to AIMS.

edges/5.description: KCNJ8/ABCC9-containing KATP channels are required cell-autonomously for brain arterial and arteriolar smooth muscle differentiation, so their loss compromises cerebral vascular maturation.

evidence.snippet: In vivo studies of abcc9 loss-of-function in zebrafish revealed an exacerbated motor response to pentylenetetrazole, a pro-convulsive drug, consistent with impaired neurodevelopment associated with an increased seizure susceptibility.
evidence.explanation: Directly ties abcc9 loss of function to increased seizure susceptibility, though the neuronal intermediates are not identified.

edges/6.description: Loss of abcc9 lowers the threshold for chemically provoked seizure-like motor activity in vivo.

evidence.snippet: Channel activation results in action potential shortening and stabilization of the resting membrane potential during the development of fatigue
evidence.explanation: Describes the protective electrical adaptation that cannot occur once the channel is lost.

edges/7.description: Without KATP opening, the fatiguing fibre cannot shorten its action potential or stabilise its resting membrane potential.

evidence.snippet: In isolated muscle, SUR2 LoF results in abnormal generation of unstimulated forces, potentially explaining painful spasms in AIMS.
evidence.explanation: Directly demonstrates unstimulated force generation in SUR2 loss-of-function muscle.

evidence.snippet: Under fatiguing conditions, isometric tetanic contraction experiments on murine extensor digitorum longus (EDL) revealed delayed loss of stimulated forces, and significant development of unstimulated forces, in muscles lacking Kir6.2 or SUR2 subunits, whereas loss of the SUR1 subunit did not impact muscle functionality.
evidence.explanation: Replicates unstimulated force development specifically in SUR2-null muscle under fatigue.

edges/8.description: Loss of KATP-dependent electrical adaptation during fatigue is followed by contraction in the absence of stimulation.

evidence.snippet: Given the roles of KATP channels in all muscles, we sought to determine how myopathy arises using tissue-selective suppression of KATP and found that LoF in skeletal muscle, specifically, underlies myopathy.
evidence.explanation: Tissue-selective suppression localises the myopathy to skeletal muscle itself.

edges/9.description: The contractile abnormality is intrinsic to skeletal muscle rather than secondary to cardiac or vascular disease.

evidence.snippet: SUR2 loss-of-function causes fatigability and cardiac dysfunction in mice, and reduced activity, cardiac dysfunction and ventricular enlargement in zebrafish.
evidence.explanation: Cardiac dysfunction follows SUR2 loss in two model organisms.

edges/10.description: Loss of cardiomyocyte KATP is followed by impaired systolic performance in patients and in both animal models.

evidence.explanation: Marked PARTIAL because the original authors advance the cerebrovascular route as a conjecture ("it is conceivable"), not a demonstrated mechanism.

evidence.snippet: These new cases further demonstrate the prominence of white matter abnormalities resembling periventricular leukomalacia or small vessel disease as a key hallmark of the disorder, alongside developmental delay, intellectual impairment, seizures, and fatigability.
evidence.explanation: The human imaging pattern is explicitly described as small-vessel-like, which is what a brain VSMC differentiation defect would predict.

edges/11.description: A cerebral small-vessel mechanism is the leading explanation for the white matter lesions, which radiologically resemble periventricular leukomalacia or small vessel disease.

evidence.snippet: and there are no reports of cognitive impairment in previous SUR2 mutant animal models.
evidence.explanation: Marked PARTIAL: the original authors state explicitly that the route from channel loss to intellectual disability is unresolved, so this edge is an association with unknown intermediates rather than a demonstrated mechanism.

edges/12.description: The cognitive phenotype tracks with the white matter burden, but no mediating cellular step has been demonstrated and a purely vascular account is not proven.

evidence.explanation: The proposed white-matter-to-hyperreflexia route, stated as a hypothesis by the authors.

edges/13.description: The authors attribute the lower-limb hyperreflexia of the older patients to the white matter abnormalities and consequent loss of upper motor neuron inhibition.

evidence.snippet: Patients are homozygous for a splice-site mutation in ABCC9 (c.1320 + 1 G > A), which encodes the sulfonylurea receptor 2 (SUR2) subunit of KATP channels.
evidence.explanation: The founding homozygous splice-site allele.

evidence.snippet: This mutation results in an in-frame deletion of exon 8, which results in non-functional KATP channels in recombinant assays.
evidence.explanation: Functional consequence of the founding allele.

evidence.snippet: According to gnomAD, the variant is reported at surprisingly high frequency in heterozygous state in the Finnish population with an allele frequency of 0.0007 (18/24850).
evidence.explanation: Population-database carrier frequency of the founding allele. Tagged OTHER because the datum is a gnomAD reference-population lookup reported by the authors, not an observation in their patient cohort.

evidence.snippet: The homozygous state is absent in gnomAD.
evidence.explanation: No homozygotes in the reference population, consistent with the biallelic genotype being disease-causing rather than a tolerated variant.

evidence.snippet: All variants are predicted to result in severe truncations or in-frame deletions within SUR2, leading to the generation of non-functional SUR2-dependent KATP channels.
evidence.explanation: Defines the allele class across seven further families.

evidence.snippet: Functional tests of recombinant channels confirm that disease-associated SUR2 truncations cause a complete loss-of-function.
evidence.explanation: Confirms complete loss of function for the truncating alleles.

evidence.snippet: Heterozygous parents do not show any conserved clinical pathology but report multiple incidences of intra-uterine fetal death, which were also observed in an eighth family included in this study.
evidence.explanation: The carrier state and the intra-uterine fetal death excess, recorded as a reproductive observation because the fetal genotypes are unknown.

evidence.snippet: All mutations were missense, and several mutations affect Arg1154.
evidence.explanation: Cited to fix the contrast, not as AIMS evidence: the ABCC9 alleles that cause Cantu syndrome are dominant missense variants clustering at Arg1154, an allele class disjoint from the biallelic truncating and splice alleles of AIMS. Marked PARTIAL because the paper is about Cantu syndrome.

evidence.snippet: These latest findings also highlight neonatal presentation of disease, deterioration following surgical procedures, and the potential for motor and cognitive decline, which should be monitored in older individuals.
evidence.explanation: Supports monitoring for decline and peri-procedural caution, but not a complete multidisciplinary-care protocol; therefore marked PARTIAL.

treatments/0.description: No AIMS-specific disease-modifying treatment is reported in the cited cohorts. The most recent cohort recommends monitoring older individuals for motor and cognitive decline and highlights deterioration following surgical procedures; manifestation-directed treatments reported elsewhere in this entry remain case-based rather than AIMS-specific protocols.

evidence.snippet: results which caution against the use of calcium channel blockers in AIMS.
evidence.explanation: The authors' explicit safety recommendation.

evidence.snippet: found that the Ca2+ channel blocker verapamil unexpectedly resulted in premature death of AIMS mice
evidence.explanation: The experimental basis for the warning.

treatments/1.description: Calcium channel blockers warrant strong caution on current preclinical evidence. Verapamil was tested in SUR2 loss-of-function mice on the hypothesis that excess CaV1.1-mediated calcium entry drove the myopathy; instead of rescuing the phenotype it caused premature death, and genetically rendering CaV1.1 non-permeable also failed to reverse the pathology. The authors state explicitly that this cautions against calcium channel blockers in AIMS. This is a model-organism safety signal, not a human trial result, and is recorded here because it is the only actionable drug-safety statement in the AIMS literature.

evidence.snippet: and walking distance in the 6-min walk test is reduced in all individuals.
evidence.explanation: Marked PARTIAL: this documents the functional deficit that physiotherapy targets, but no study has tested physiotherapy in AIMS.

treatments/2.description: Physiotherapy and graded, paced activity address the fatigability, balance deficits and reduced walking distance objectively documented in the index cohort. No trial evidence exists in AIMS; this is standard neuromuscular rehabilitation applied to a documented functional deficit.

evidence.snippet: antagonist and a beta-blocker was started.
evidence.explanation: Records the treatment actually given. The quoted span begins at "antagonist" because the preceding "Treatment with an ACE-" is broken across a hyphenated PDF line break in the cached full text.

evidence.snippet: Cardiac systolic dysfunction is found in the two oldest patients.
evidence.explanation: The indication - the age-related cardiac complication this therapy targets.

treatments/3.description: Standard heart-failure pharmacotherapy for the reduced systolic function that emerges in older individuals: an ACE inhibitor plus a beta-blocker was started in the index patient found to have biventricular systolic dysfunction with an ejection fraction of 35-40%. This is a single reported case managed by conventional heart-failure practice, not an AIMS-specific regimen, and no outcome is reported. Note the direction-of-effect contrast with Cantu syndrome, where ACE inhibitors appear on the GeneReviews agents-to-avoid list because they open KATP channels that are already overactive; in AIMS the channels carry no measurable current, so that rationale does not transfer.

evidence.snippet: Lamotrigine treatment was partly effective.
evidence.explanation: The one reported anti-seizure drug outcome in AIMS: partial efficacy of lamotrigine in the index patient with tonic and tonic-clonic episodes. This is the sentence that supports the lamotrigine claim in the description.

evidence.snippet: Affected individuals show psychomotor delay and intellectual disability of variable severity, microcephaly, corpus callosum and white matter abnormalities, seizures, spasticity, short stature, muscle fatigability and weakness.
evidence.explanation: Marked PARTIAL and retained only to establish that seizures recur across the expanded cohort and therefore need treatment; this cohort reports no drug-specific outcomes.

treatments/4.description: Anti-seizure medication for patients with documented seizures. In the index cohort lamotrigine was partly effective in the one patient with recurrent tonic and tonic-clonic episodes. No AIMS-specific anti-seizure drug choice has been established.

evidence.snippet: it is conceivable that KATP loss of function may impact the cerebral vasculature
evidence.explanation: The authors' own statement of the hypothesis, framed as a conjecture.

evidence.snippet: Interestingly, white matter hyperintensities are observed in both Cantú syndrome and AIMS.
evidence.explanation: That the same white matter change appears in the gain-of-function disease is what makes a shared cerebrovascular route plausible, but it also means the finding does not discriminate direction of effect.

evidence.snippet: Our results demonstrate a role for KCNJ8/ABCC9-containing K-ATP channels in the differentiation of brain VSMC, which in turn is necessary for fine-tuning of cerebral blood flow.
evidence.explanation: Supplies the developmental cerebrovascular role, but in animal and cell models rather than AIMS patients.

hypotheses/0.description: The leading explanation for the CNS arm of AIMS is that loss of SUR2-containing KATP channels in brain vascular smooth muscle degrades cerebral autoregulation and neurovascular coupling, producing chronic small-vessel ischaemic white matter injury and, through it, the intellectual disability and pyramidal signs. The supporting facts are consistent but indirect: KCNJ8/ABCC9-containing channels are required for brain vascular smooth muscle differentiation in animals, the human imaging resembles small vessel disease, MR angiography is normal so the lesion is functional rather than macrovascular, and the same white matter change is seen in Cantu syndrome where the channel defect is opposite. What is missing is any direct measurement of cerebral blood flow or neurovascular coupling in an AIMS patient, and the in vivo coupling deficit was demonstrated in a Kcnj8 rather than an Abcc9 knockout. The original authors state the hypothesis with the hedge "it is conceivable".

evidence.snippet: We sought to determine whether excessive Ca2+ influx through CaV 1.1 channels was responsible for myopathology but found that the Ca2+ channel blocker verapamil unexpectedly resulted in premature death of AIMS mice and that rendering CaV 1.1 channels nonpermeable by mutation failed to reverse pathology; results which caution against the use of calcium channel blockers in AIMS.
evidence.explanation: Direct pharmacologic and genetic tests failed to support CaV1.1-mediated calcium influx as the cause of the myopathy; the drug intervention was additionally harmful.

hypotheses/1.description: Excessive calcium influx through skeletal-muscle CaV1.1 channels was tested as the downstream cause of the SUR2 loss-of-function myopathy. The model is not retained as the current mechanism: making CaV1.1 non-permeable did not reverse the pathology, while verapamil caused premature death in AIMS mice. The directly observed unstimulated-force phenotype remains established, but its downstream effector is unresolved.

evidence.snippet: nor in tests of spatial learning and memory, evaluated using a Morris water maze
evidence.explanation: The mouse spatial-learning result is formally negative.

evidence.snippet: show any obvious anxiety-like behaviors.
evidence.explanation: The mouse anxiety result is likewise negative, against a human phenotype that includes anxiety.

evidence.snippet: and there are no reports of cognitive impairment in previous SUR2 mutant animal models.
evidence.explanation: The authors state, in the same sentence, both that the route from channel loss to intellectual disability is not obvious and that no earlier SUR2 mutant animal model showed cognitive impairment.

open_questions/0.rationale: This is a model-evidence-exists-and-is-negative situation, not an absence of data. The SUR2-STOP mouse was formally tested for spatial learning and memory in a Morris water maze and for anxiety-like behaviour in an elevated plus maze and was negative on both, while every human patient tested has intellectual disability and several have anxiety. The original authors also note that it is not obvious how myocyte KATP dysfunction could produce intellectual disability at all, and that neuronal KATP channels are predominantly Kir6.2/SUR1 rather than SUR2-containing. Together these make the cognitive arm the least secure part of the AIMS mechanism: either the murine assays are too coarse for a mild human intellectual disability, or the human cognitive phenotype is mediated by something (most plausibly the cerebrovascular route) that the mouse does not reproduce.

evidence.snippet: These latest findings also highlight neonatal presentation of disease, deterioration following surgical procedures, and the potential for motor and cognitive decline, which should be monitored in older individuals.
evidence.explanation: The most recent series calls for monitoring of older individuals without being able to specify what or how often, which is the gap.

open_questions/1.rationale: Around twenty patients have ever been reported, in three cross-sectional series with no prospective follow-up. Two features are known to be age-dependent - systolic dysfunction, present only in the oldest patients of the index cohort, and cognitive and motor decline reported in a sexagenarian - but neither has a defined onset distribution, so no surveillance interval can be evidence-based. No registry, survival analysis, or quality-of-life instrument has ever been applied.

evidence.snippet: Mutant (P182L) but not wild-type HSPB1 led to the formation of insoluble intracellular aggregates and to the sequestration in the cytoplasm of selective cellular components, including neurofilament middle chain subunit (NF-M) and p150 dynactin.
evidence.explanation: Shows that a mutant HSPB1 allele aggregates and sequesters neurofilament and dynactin subunits in primary neurons.

evidence.snippet: In motor neurons, expression of both HSPB8 K141N and K141E mutations clearly resulted in neurite degeneration
evidence.explanation: Shows that the CMT2L HSPB8 alleles degenerate neurites in motor neurons.

steps/27.description: Mutations in the alpha-crystallin domain of the small heat-shock proteins HSPB1 (HSP27) and HSPB8 (HSP22) convert them from chaperones into aggregation-prone proteins. Mutant HSP27 forms insoluble intracellular aggregates that sequester neurofilament middle chain and the p150 subunit of dynactin, and mutant HSP22 degenerates neurites selectively in motor neurons while leaving sensory and cortical neurons and glial cells largely unaffected. Alleles of both genes are reported in axonal CMT2 and in distal hereditary motor neuropathy.

evidence.snippet: Aminoacylation and yeast viability assays showed that p.Arg329His AARS severely reduces enzyme activity.
evidence.explanation: Direct assay evidence that the CMT2N allele loses aminoacylation activity.

evidence.snippet: p.Ala397Thr MARS supported very little yeast cell growth, consistent with this being a loss-of-function allele.
evidence.explanation: Yeast complementation evidence that the CMT2U allele loses methionyl-tRNA synthetase function.

steps/28.description: Cytoplasmic aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases charge tRNAs with their amino acid. Dominant CMT2 alleles of AARS1 (CMT2N) and MARS1 (CMT2U) behave as loss-of-function in aminoacylation and yeast complementation assays, and the resulting peripheral phenotype is a length-dependent axonal degeneration without central features. The GARS1 disease CMT2D is modeled separately in this entry, because its alleles act through aberrant new interactions rather than through the charging deficit alone.

evidence.snippet: DHTKD1 silencing was found to lead to impaired energy production, evidenced by decreased ATP, total NAD
evidence.explanation: Direct measurement that loss of DHTKD1 lowers cellular ATP and NAD(H).

evidence.snippet: This gene codes for dehydrogenase E1 and transketolase domain-containing protein 1, which is part of a 2-oxoglutarate-dehydrogenase-complex-like protein.
evidence.explanation: Source for the description of what DHTKD1 encodes, as stated in this node.

evidence.snippet: Increased levels of 2-oxoadipate in individual-derived fibroblasts normalized upon lentiviral expression of the wild-type DHTKD1 mRNA.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the metabolic step DHTKD1 loss blocks, by rescue in patient fibroblasts.

steps/29.description: DHTKD1, the gene behind dominant CMT2Q, is part of a 2-oxoglutarate-dehydrogenase-complex-like protein and acts inside the mitochondrion rather than on its shape or transport. Silencing it lowers cellular ATP and NAD(H), and expressing wild-type DHTKD1 in patient fibroblasts normalizes the 2-oxoadipate that accumulates without it.

evidence.snippet: MPV17 encodes a putative channel-forming protein of the inner mitochondrial membrane and is involved in mitochondrial deoxynucleotide homeostasis.
evidence.explanation: States the mitochondrial role of MPV17 that this node describes.

evidence.snippet: Here, we describe five additional patients from two unrelated families with sensorimotor axonal neuropathy without hepatocerebral affection caused by homozygous MPV17 variants.
evidence.explanation: The patients in whom the MPV17 defect produced neuropathy alone.

steps/30.description: MPV17 is an inner mitochondrial membrane protein serving mitochondrial deoxynucleotide homeostasis. Biallelic MPV17 variants were first described in a mitochondrial DNA depletion syndrome with early-onset liver failure, and can also present as an isolated axonal sensorimotor neuropathy with no liver or brain involvement, which is CMT2EE.

evidence.snippet: Immunostaining peripheral nerve axons localized ATP1A1 to the axolemma of myelinated sensory and motor axons and to Schmidt-Lanterman incisures of myelin sheaths.
evidence.explanation: Places ATP1A1 at the axolemma, the site this node describes.

evidence.snippet: demonstrated significant reduction in Na+ current activity in some, but not all, ouabain-insensitive ATP1A1 mutants, suggesting a loss-of-function defect of the Na+,K+ pump
evidence.explanation: Two-electrode voltage clamp evidence of reduced pump current, with the authors' own caveat that not all mutants behaved this way.

steps/31.description: ATP1A1 encodes the alpha-1 subunit of the Na+,K+-ATPase and is present on the axolemma of myelinated sensory and motor axons and at Schmidt-Lanterman incisures. Several CMT2DD substitutions reduce pump current in a heterologous expression system, pointing to a loss-of-function defect in the sodium-potassium pump.

evidence.snippet: Our studies of mutant protein posttranslational modification and localization indicated that the mutations (p.Ser577Arg, p.Ser650Pro) impair protein glycosylation and reduce JAG1 cell surface expression.
evidence.explanation: Supports impaired glycosylation and reduced surface delivery of the Notch ligand as the molecular lesion.

evidence.snippet: Mice harboring heterozygous CMT2-associated mutations exhibited mild peripheral neuropathy, and homozygous expression resulted in embryonic lethality by midgestation.
evidence.explanation: Model-organism support that the heterozygous CMT2 alleles produce peripheral neuropathy.

steps/32.description: JAG1 encodes the canonical Notch ligand Jagged1. The two reported CMT2HH missense variants (p.Ser577Arg, p.Ser650Pro) impair post-translational glycosylation of the protein and reduce the amount of JAG1 reaching the cell surface, where it would otherwise engage Notch receptors on neighbouring cells. Mice heterozygous for the CMT2-associated alleles develop mild peripheral neuropathy.

evidence.snippet: Modelling of the mutant KCC3 cotransporter in Xenopus oocytes showed a significant reduction in potassium influx for both changes.
evidence.explanation: Direct functional measurement of reduced cotransporter activity for the two de novo variants.

evidence.snippet: We identified heterozygous de novo variants in SLC12A6 in three unrelated patients with intermediate CMT.

steps/33.description: SLC12A6 encodes KCC3, a potassium-chloride cotransporter. Dominantly acting de novo missense variants reduce potassium influx through the mutant cotransporter when expressed in Xenopus oocytes. How reduced KCC3 transport injures the peripheral nerve is not established; the largest dominant SLC12A6 cohort states that more work is needed to understand the mechanism, and this node therefore records the measured transport deficit rather than a downstream nerve mechanism.

evidence.snippet: In vitro biochemical and cellular assays revealed that patient variants impair the GTPase-activating protein (GAP) activity of ARHGAP19 and reduce ARHGAP19 protein levels.
evidence.explanation: Supports loss of GAP activity and reduced protein level as the molecular lesion.

evidence.snippet: LOF in ARHGAP19 orthologues in Drosophila melanogaster and Danio rerio induced motor defects in axonal and synaptic morphology.
evidence.explanation: Model-organism support that loss of function produces axonal and synaptic pathology.

steps/34.description: ARHGAP19 is a GTPase-activating protein that switches RhoA off by stimulating its intrinsic GTP hydrolysis. Biallelic CMT2KK variants both lower ARHGAP19 protein levels and impair its GAP activity, a loss-of-function mechanism. Loss of the orthologue in Drosophila and zebrafish produces motor defects with abnormal axonal and synaptic morphology, and patient-derived motor neurons show the same cellular phenotypes.

evidence.snippet: The mutant protein impairs Complex IV assembly and activity, leading to a reduction in mitochondrial membrane potential.
evidence.explanation: Supports impaired complex IV assembly and activity as the molecular lesion in this node.

evidence.snippet: Downregulation of the COX18 homologue in D. melanogaster resulted in signs of neurodegeneration, including locomotor deficit and progressive axonal degeneration of sensory neurons.
evidence.explanation: Model-organism support linking COX18 loss to progressive axonal degeneration of sensory neurons.

steps/35.description: COX18 translocates the C-terminal tail of MTCO2 across the mitochondrial inner membrane during assembly of respiratory chain complex IV. The reported CMT2MM splice variant produces a stable but defective COX18 isoform lacking exon 2, which impairs complex IV assembly and activity and lowers the mitochondrial membrane potential. This is a primary respiratory-chain lesion, distinct from the mitochondrial-dynamics lesions of MFN2 and GDAP1 curated above.

evidence.snippet: Functional studies revealed reduced DARS2 protein levels, mitochondrial network abnormalities, and impaired mitochondrial function.
evidence.explanation: Supports reduced DARS2 protein and impaired mitochondrial function as the molecular lesion.

evidence.snippet: p.Ser238Phe behaves as a hypomorphic allele, whereas p.Pro503Leu reduced DARS2 enzymatic activity by 75%.
evidence.explanation: Quantifies the enzymatic deficit and supports the hypomorphic-allele model in this node's description.

steps/36.description: DARS2 encodes the mitochondrial aspartyl-tRNA synthetase. Biallelic variants that pair a hypomorphic allele with a more deleterious one lower DARS2 protein levels and impair mitochondrial function without producing the leukoencephalopathy (LBSL) associated with more severe allele combinations. One reported variant reduced DARS2 enzymatic activity by 75 percent in HEK293 cells.

evidence.snippet: A causal relationship between Mitofusin (MFN) 2 gene mutations and the hereditary axonal neuropathy Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2A (CMT2A) was described over 15 years ago.
evidence.explanation: Review establishes MFN2 as the causal gene for CMT2A and its role in mitochondrial fusion.

evidence.snippet: MFN2 loss did not affect spinal motor neuron differentiation from hESCs but resulted in mitochondrial fragmentation and dysfunction as determined by live-cell imaging.
evidence.explanation: In vitro evidence that MFN2 deficiency causes mitochondrial fragmentation in human motor neurons.

steps/37.description: MFN2 mutations impair mitochondrial outer membrane fusion, leading to fragmented mitochondria. Loss of fusion capacity prevents complementation of damaged mitochondrial DNA and proteins, resulting in dysfunctional mitochondrial networks in neurons.

evidence.snippet: MFN2 deficit impaired anterograde and retrograde mitochondrial transport within axons, and reduced the mRNA and protein levels of kinesin and dynein, indicating the interfered motor protein expression induced by MFN2 deficiency.
evidence.explanation: Direct demonstration that MFN2 loss impairs bidirectional mitochondrial transport in human motor neuron axons.

steps/38.description: Fragmented mitochondria resulting from MFN2 dysfunction fail to be efficiently transported to distal axon terminals. MFN2 also directly regulates mitochondrial transport by interacting with the Miro/Milton motor adaptor complex. Energy deficits at distal terminals result from inadequate mitochondrial delivery.

evidence.snippet: Both mutations disrupted the self-assembly of human NFL.
evidence.explanation: Direct demonstration that CMT2E NEFL mutations (P8R and Q333P) disrupt neurofilament assembly in cultured cells.

evidence.snippet: Diseased motor neurons recapitulated known pathologic phenotypes at early time points of differentiation, including aberrant accumulation of neurofilament light chain protein in neuronal cell bodies.
evidence.explanation: iPSC-derived motor neurons from CMT2E patient with NEFL N98S mutation show neurofilament accumulation, directly linking NEFL mutations to neurofilament assembly disruption.

evidence.snippet: the p.N98S mutation causes a profound reduction of neurofilaments in the myelinated axons of the PNS and CNS, resulting in substantially reduced axonal diameters, particularly of large myelinated axons, and distal axon loss in the PNS.
evidence.explanation: Mouse model of CMT2E with heterozygous Nefl N98S mutation confirms neurofilament reduction in axons and distal axon loss.

evidence.snippet: Consistently, we show that these mutations cause protein aggregation which are recognised by the autophagic pathway in motoneurons and triggered caspase 3 activation leading to apoptosis in neuroblastoma cells.
evidence.explanation: CMT2CC NEFH frameshift products aggregate in motoneurons and kill neuroblastoma cells, the NEFH arm of this node.

evidence.snippet: Trim2-gene trap mice showed axonopathy with accumulations of neurofilaments inside axons.
evidence.explanation: Loss of the TRIM2 ligase produces intra-axonal neurofilament accumulation, the CMT2R arm of this node.

evidence.snippet: TRIM2 is an E3 ubiquitin ligase that ubiquitinates neurofilament light chain, a component of the intermediate filament in axons.
evidence.explanation: States the substrate relationship that makes TRIM2 loss a neurofilament-handling defect.

evidence.snippet: This mutation results in decreased DDB1-DCAF8 association, leading to an E3 ubiquitin ligase defect that is likely associated with neurofilament degradation.
evidence.explanation: Co-immunoprecipitation evidence that the GAN2 DCAF8 allele weakens the Cullin-4 ligase that turns neurofilaments over.

evidence.snippet: Giant axons with neurofilament accumulations were found in 3 affected persons who had undergone nerve biopsy evaluations.
evidence.explanation: Nerve-biopsy confirmation that neurofilaments accumulate in axons of DCAF8 patients.

steps/39.description: The axonal neurofilament network is disrupted in several CMT2 subtypes, by mutation of a neurofilament subunit or by loss of the ubiquitin ligases that turn neurofilaments over. NEFL mutations cause abnormal neurofilament assembly and accumulation of neurofilament aggregates in neuronal cell bodies and proximal axons. Disrupted neurofilament stoichiometry impairs axonal caliber maintenance and reduces neurofilament density in myelinated axons, particularly affecting large-caliber fibers. NEFH frameshift alleles that read through into the 3' UTR append a cryptic amyloidogenic element, and the resulting protein aggregates. Loss of TRIM2 or weakened assembly of the Cullin-4 ligase complex through DCAF8 removes the degradation arm instead, so neurofilaments accumulate inside axons and, for DCAF8, produce the giant axons that name GAN2.

evidence.snippet: In Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease 2B (CMT2B), a neuropathy of the peripheral nervous system, this tubulating mechanism is disrupted.
evidence.explanation: Demonstrates that CMT2B RAB7A mutations disrupt endosomal tubulation and TrkA neurotrophin receptor retrieval.

evidence.snippet: Missense mutations in RAB7A, the gene encoding the small GTPase Rab7, cause CMT2B and increase Rab7 activity. Rab7 is ubiquitously expressed and is involved in degradation through the lysosomal pathway.
evidence.explanation: Drosophila model confirms RAB7A mutations cause CMT2B through altered endosomal/lysosomal trafficking with sensory and motor phenotypes.

steps/40.description: RAB7A mutations impair late endosomal trafficking and lysosomal degradation in neurons. Defective endosome-to-lysosome maturation disrupts neurotrophin receptor signaling and cellular waste removal in long axons, particularly sensory neurons.

evidence.snippet: Through intravital imaging of the sciatic nerve, we show that CMT2D mice displayed early and persistent disturbances in axonal transport of neurotrophin-containing signaling endosomes in vivo.
evidence.explanation: Directly supports impaired neurotrophin signaling endosome axonal transport in CMT2D mice.

evidence.snippet: (BDNF)/TrkB impairments correlated with transport disruption and overall CMT2D neuropathology and that inhibition of this pathway at the nerve-muscle interface perturbed endosome transport in wild-type axons.
evidence.explanation: Links BDNF/TrkB pathway impairment to transport disruption and CMT2D neuropathology.

steps/41.description: GARS1 gain-of-function mutations produce toxic glycyl-tRNA synthetase variants that aberrantly interact with neurotrophin receptor pathways such as BDNF/TrkB. In CMT2D models, this disrupts axonal transport of neurotrophin-containing signaling endosomes, compromising trophic signaling in long peripheral axons.

evidence.snippet: In patient-derived fibroblasts, we found a complete loss of SORD protein and increased intracellular sorbitol.
evidence.explanation: Patient-derived fibroblast evidence supports SORD protein loss and intracellular sorbitol accumulation.

evidence.snippet: In Drosophila, loss of SORD orthologs caused synaptic degeneration and progressive motor impairment.
evidence.explanation: Model-organism evidence links SORD deficiency to synaptic degeneration and progressive motor impairment.

steps/42.description: Biallelic SORD loss-of-function variants reduce sorbitol dehydrogenase activity in the polyol pathway. Loss of SORD protein causes intracellular and serum sorbitol accumulation, which is linked to peripheral axon degeneration in patient cells and Drosophila models.

evidence.snippet: Functional studies showed that the Glu185Lys variant impaired autophagic function leading to the accumulation of immature autophagosomes.
evidence.explanation: Direct functional evidence that the CMT2Y VCP allele blocks autophagosome maturation.

evidence.snippet: the loss of spatacsin leads to the accumulation of lipids in lysosomes by perturbing their clearance from these organelles
evidence.explanation: Establishes the lysosomal clearance defect caused by loss of the CMT2X gene product.

steps/43.description: Two CMT2 genes converge on the autophagy-lysosome arm of protein and lipid clearance. The CMT2Y VCP allele leaves immature autophagosomes accumulating, and loss of the CMT2X gene product spatacsin leaves lipids uncleared from lysosomes, with motor neuron degeneration in the knockout mouse.

evidence.snippet: The finding of site-specific amino acid substitutions in limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 1B, autosomal dominant Emery-Dreifuss muscular dystrophy, dilated cardiomyopathy type 1A, autosomal dominant partial lipodystrophy, and, now, AR-CMT2 suggests the existence of distinct functional domains
evidence.explanation: Places the CMT2B1 allele among the LMNA diseases, supporting a lamina defect as the node's substrate.

steps/44.description: Lamin A/C is a component of the nuclear envelope. A homozygous LMNA founder allele causes autosomal recessive axonal CMT2B1, and sciatic nerves of lamin-A/C-null mice show the loss of axons, axonal enlargement and unmyelinated profiles seen in human peripheral axonopathy.

evidence.snippet: GDAP1 truncations that are found in patients who have CMT are not targeted to mitochondria and have lost mitochondrial fragmentation activity.
evidence.explanation: Patient-derived GDAP1 truncations lose the fission activity this node describes.

evidence.snippet: GDAP1 is located in the mitochondrial outer membrane and regulates the mitochondrial network.
evidence.explanation: Localizes GDAP1 and states the process it regulates.

steps/45.description: GDAP1 sits in the mitochondrial outer membrane and drives fission of the mitochondrial network. CMT-associated truncations fail to reach mitochondria and lose fragmentation activity, and point mutations reduce it strongly, so the GDAP1 defect is a loss of fission rather than the loss of fusion produced by MFN2. Both leave the mitochondrial network mishandled, which is why GDAP1 is wired to its own node rather than to Mitochondrial Fragmentation.

evidence.snippet: In the peripheral nerve, axon-Schwann cell interaction is essential for the structural organization of myelinated fibres and is primarily mediated by the binding of CADM3, expressed in axons, to CADM4, expressed by myelinating Schwann cells.
evidence.explanation: States the CADM3-CADM4 axon-glia adhesion pairing that this node asserts is disrupted.

evidence.snippet: Our data support a retention of the mutant protein in the endoplasmic reticulum and reduced cell surface expression in vitro.
evidence.explanation: Supports loss of CADM3 from the axonal surface as the proximate molecular lesion.

evidence.snippet: Our findings indicate the involvement of abnormal axon-glia interaction as a disease-causing mechanism in CMT patients with CADM3 mutations.
evidence.explanation: The authors' own statement that abnormal axon-glia interaction is the disease mechanism in CADM3 CMT.

steps/46.description: CADM3 is expressed on the axon and binds CADM4 on the myelinating Schwann cell; this pairing organizes the myelinated fibre at the axon-glia interface. The recurrent CMT2FF variant Tyr172Cys introduces a new disulphide bond, retains the mutant protein in the endoplasmic reticulum, reduces its surface expression and lowers its co-localization with CADM4 at intercellular contacts. Knock-in mice show normal nerve conduction and myelin morphology but disordered axonal organization, so the lesion is an adhesion and domain-organization defect in an otherwise normally myelinated axon rather than a demyelinating one.

evidence.snippet: Genetic neuropathies that primarily cause axonal degeneration, as opposed to demyelination, are most often classified as Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2 (CMT2) and are the focus of this review.
evidence.explanation: Authoritative review establishing CMT2 as defined by axonal degeneration rather than demyelination.

evidence.snippet: the challenge of defining the central underlying mechanism(s) linking mitochondrial abnormalities to progressive dying-back of peripheral arm and leg nerves in CMT2A is largely unmet
evidence.explanation: Confirms the dying-back pattern of axonal degeneration as the hallmark of CMT2A pathology.

steps/47.description: The final common pathway in CMT2 involves dying-back degeneration of peripheral nerve axons. The longest axons are affected first due to their higher metabolic and transport demands, producing the characteristic length-dependent pattern of weakness and sensory loss. This is a Wallerian-like process distinct from neuronal apoptosis.

evidence.snippet: Inherited peripheral neuropathies are a genetically and phenotypically diverse group of disorders that lead to degeneration of peripheral neurons with resulting sensory and motor dysfunction.
evidence.explanation: Review confirms motor dysfunction as a core feature of inherited axonal neuropathies including CMT2.

steps/48.description: Progressive weakness of distal limb muscles, particularly affecting the peroneal muscles of the lower legs and intrinsic hand muscles. Leads to difficulty with foot dorsiflexion (foot drop) and fine motor tasks.

evidence.snippet: It is characterised by prominent sensory loss, often complicated by severe ulcero-mutilations of toes or feet, and variable motor involvement.
evidence.explanation: Clinical characterization of CMT2B from the introduction of the paper, describing the human phenotype.

steps/49.description: Progressive sensory loss in a stocking-glove distribution, affecting vibration and proprioception more than pain and temperature in most subtypes.

evidence.snippet: As the disease progresses, individuals often develop foot drop and foot deformities such as pes cavus and equinus, leading to a significant decline in gait function.
evidence.explanation: Review confirms pes cavus as a hallmark foot deformity in CMT.

steps/50.description: High-arched feet (pes cavus) resulting from imbalance between intrinsic and extrinsic foot muscles. Often accompanied by hammer toes and equinovarus deformity.

evidence.snippet: All patients presented with distal weakness and atrophy in the lower limb, two of whom had minor clinical sensory abnormalities and small fiber neuropathy.
evidence.explanation: In an axonal CMT2 (SORD) clinical series, all patients had distal lower-limb weakness and atrophy, directly supporting distal lower-limb amyotrophy as a core CMT2 phenotype.

steps/51.description: Wasting of distal leg muscles producing the characteristic inverted champagne bottle or stork leg appearance.

steps/52.description: Absent or reduced deep tendon reflexes, particularly at the ankles, reflecting loss of the afferent sensory arc.

evidence.snippet: One of the hallmark manifestations of CMT is gait disturbance. As the disease progresses, individuals often develop foot drop and foot deformities such as pes cavus and equinus, leading to a significant decline in gait function.
evidence.explanation: Review confirms gait disturbance including foot drop as a hallmark of CMT.

steps/53.description: Characteristic high-stepping gait due to foot drop from peroneal muscle weakness, requiring exaggerated hip and knee flexion during the swing phase of walking.

steps/54.description: Weakness of intrinsic hand muscles developing later in the disease course, affecting grip strength and fine motor skills.

edges/30.description: Fragmented mitochondria cannot be efficiently transported along axons, as mitofusin-2 also plays a direct role in mitochondrial motility and attachment to motor proteins.

edges/31.description: Failure of mitochondrial delivery to distal axon terminals causes energy failure and triggers length-dependent axonal degeneration.

edges/32.description: Disrupted neurofilament network impairs axonal caliber and slow axonal transport, contributing to axonal degeneration.

edges/33.description: Defective endosomal trafficking impairs neurotrophin receptor signaling and autophagy, leading to sensory axon degeneration.

edges/34.description: Persistent disruption of neurotrophin signaling endosome transport deprives long axons of trophic support and contributes to distal axonal degeneration.

edges/35.description: Sorbitol accumulation and polyol-pathway dysfunction contribute to the length-dependent peripheral axon degeneration seen in SORD-CMT2.

evidence.snippet: These findings suggest a possible pathogenic mechanism for HSPB1 whereby the mutation may lead to preferential motor neuron loss by disrupting selective components essential for axonal structure and transport.
evidence.explanation: Proposes the sequestration-to-axonal-failure step this edge asserts.

edges/36.description: Sequestration of neurofilament and dynactin subunits into mutant small-heat-shock-protein aggregates removes components required for axonal structure and transport, and mutant HSPB8 degenerates neurites directly.

evidence.snippet: Patients present with sensory-motor distal degeneration secondary to predominant axonal neuropathy, slight demyelination, and no atypical or additional CNS features.
evidence.explanation: Describes the distal axonal degeneration that follows the AARS1 charging deficit in patients.

edges/37.description: Reduced tRNA charging in long peripheral neurons is followed by distal-predominant axonal degeneration, with the central nervous system spared.

evidence.snippet: Spinal motor neurons also degenerated and this was accompanied by fragmentation of neuromuscular junctions and muscle atrophy.
evidence.explanation: Spatacsin-null mice degenerate spinal motor neurons and their neuromuscular junctions, the degeneration step of this edge.

edges/38.description: Failure of autophagic and lysosomal clearance in long neurons is followed by axonal and motor neuron degeneration.

evidence.snippet: Ultrastructural exploration of sciatic nerves of LMNA null (i.e., -/-) mice was performed and revealed a strong reduction of axon density, axonal enlargement, and the presence of nonmyelinated axons, all of which were highly similar to the phenotypes of human peripheral axonopathies.
evidence.explanation: Sciatic-nerve ultrastructure in the lamin-A/C-null mouse, the degeneration step of this edge.

edges/39.description: Absence of lamin A/C is followed by axonal loss and enlargement in peripheral nerve.

evidence.snippet: implicating an important role for DHTKD1 in mitochondrial energy production and neurological development
evidence.explanation: The authors' own conclusion tying the DHTKD1 energy defect to the neurological phenotype.

edges/40.description: Reduced mitochondrial energy output leaves the longest peripheral axons, which have the largest transport and metabolic demand, unable to sustain their distal segments.

evidence.snippet: This report provides further evidence that MPV17 mutations should be considered in patients with pure, non-syndromic axonal neuropathy.
evidence.explanation: Establishes that the MPV17 defect can present as an isolated axonal neuropathy.

edges/41.description: Biallelic MPV17 variants can produce a pure axonal sensorimotor neuropathy, with none of the hepatic or cerebral disease the same gene causes in its depletion-syndrome presentation.

evidence.snippet: Our data indicate that an exquisitely tight control of mitochondrial dynamics, regulated by GDAP1, is crucial for the proper function of myelinated peripheral nerves.
evidence.explanation: States the step from disturbed GDAP1-controlled mitochondrial dynamics to peripheral nerve dysfunction.

edges/42.description: Loss of control over mitochondrial network dynamics compromises the function of myelinated peripheral nerve and contributes to the axonal degeneration of CMT2K.

evidence.snippet: These findings identify a CMT pathway and a potential target for therapy development in degenerative diseases of peripheral nerve axons.
evidence.explanation: The authors' own framing of the ATP1A1 defect as a degenerative pathway in peripheral nerve axons.

edges/43.description: A weakened axonal sodium-potassium pump is proposed as a degenerative pathway in peripheral nerve axons and a candidate therapeutic target.

edges/44.description: Loss of the CADM3-CADM4 adhesion pairing disorganizes the myelinated axon and converges on the shared length-dependent axonal degeneration of CMT2.

edges/45.description: Reduced Jagged1 availability at the cell surface compromises peripheral nerve integrity, particularly of the recurrent laryngeal nerve, and converges on the shared axonal degeneration of CMT2.

edges/46.description: Reduced KCC3 cotransport precedes the length-dependent sensorimotor neuropathy seen in these patients; the intervening steps are not established, so the link is recorded as indirect with unknown intermediates.

edges/47.description: Failure to inactivate RhoA disrupts axonal and synaptic morphology in motor neurons, converging on the shared motor-predominant axonal degeneration of this subtype.

edges/48.description: Reduced complex IV assembly and activity produces a bioenergetic deficit in the axon and, in the fly model, progressive axonal degeneration of sensory neurons.

edges/49.description: Partial loss of mitochondrial aspartyl-tRNA aminoacylation impairs mitochondrial function and converges on the length-dependent axonal degeneration seen in these individuals.

evidence.snippet: A causal relationship between Mitofusin (MFN) 2 gene mutations and the hereditary axonal neuropathy Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2A (CMT2A) was described over 15 years ago.
evidence.explanation: Establishes MFN2 as the causal gene for CMT2A.

evidence.snippet: Here, we demonstrate that allele-specific CRISPR gene editing in a human model of axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth (CMT) disease rescues pathology caused by a dominant missense mutation in the neurofilament light chain gene (NEFL, CMT type 2E).
evidence.explanation: Patient-derived motor neuron evidence confirms a dominant NEFL missense mutation as causal for CMT2E pathology.

evidence.snippet: NEFL | HGNC:7739 | Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2 | MONDO:0018993 | AR | Definitive
evidence.explanation: ClinGen classifies the NEFL-Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2 gene-disease relationship as definitive with autosomal recessive inheritance.

genes/1.notes: Both dominant missense and recessive null mutations described causing CMT2E

evidence.snippet: Missense mutations in RAB7A, the gene encoding the small GTPase Rab7, cause CMT2B and increase Rab7 activity.
evidence.explanation: Confirms RAB7A mutations are causal for CMT2B.

evidence.snippet: RAB7A | HGNC:9788 | Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2 | MONDO:0018993 | AD | Definitive
evidence.explanation: ClinGen classifies the RAB7A-Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2 gene-disease relationship as definitive with autosomal dominant inheritance.

genes/2.notes: RAB7A regulates late endosomal and lysosomal trafficking; mutations cause CMT2B with prominent sensory involvement

evidence.snippet: Aberrant interactions between GlyRS mutants and different proteins, including neurotrophin receptor tropomyosin receptor kinase receptor B (TrkB), underlie CMT type 2D (CMT2D); however, our pathomechanistic understanding of this untreatable peripheral neuropathy remains incomplete.
evidence.explanation: Supports GARS1/GlyRS mutant pathology as the causal basis of CMT2D.

genes/3.notes: Encodes glycyl-tRNA synthetase; mutations cause CMT2D with predominantly upper extremity involvement

evidence.snippet: The MPZ mutation Asp121Asn may be associated with late-onset axonal neuropathy, early onset hearing loss and pupil abnormalities.
evidence.explanation: Human family evidence supports MPZ mutation association with late-onset axonal CMT2I/J features.

genes/4.notes: Myelin protein zero mutations can cause late-onset axonal CMT2I/J with pupillary abnormalities

evidence.snippet: Here we report biallelic mutations in the sorbitol dehydrogenase gene (SORD) as the most frequent recessive form of hereditary neuropathy.
evidence.explanation: Establishes biallelic SORD variants as causative for an autosomal recessive hereditary neuropathy in the CMT2 spectrum.

genes/5.notes: Biallelic SORD loss-of-function variants cause autosomal recessive SORD-related axonal CMT2 / distal hereditary motor neuropathy.

evidence.snippet: Here we report a missense mutation in the gene encoding 27-kDa small heat-shock protein B1 (HSPB1, also called HSP27) that segregates in the family with CMT2F.
evidence.explanation: Establishes HSPB1 (HSP27) as causative for axonal CMT2F.

genes/6.notes: Encodes the small heat-shock protein HSP27; dominant mutations cause axonal CMT2F and overlap with distal hereditary motor neuropathy.

evidence.snippet: Here we present a new axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease form, associated with the gene microrchidia family CW-type zinc finger 2 (MORC2).
evidence.explanation: Establishes MORC2 as causative for axonal CMT2Z.

genes/7.notes: Encodes a CW-type zinc finger transcriptional regulator; mutations cause axonal CMT2Z with a clinically heterogeneous, sometimes SMA-like, phenotype.

evidence.snippet: Mutations in GDAP1 associate with demyelinating (CMT4A) and axonal (CMT2K) forms of CMT.
evidence.explanation: Establishes GDAP1 as causative for axonal CMT2K.

genes/8.notes: Regulates mitochondrial fission; mutations cause both demyelinating CMT4A and axonal CMT2K (recessive and dominant).

evidence.snippet: gene was recently identified to cause autosomal dominant axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease (CMT2cc)
evidence.explanation: Establishes NEFH as causative for autosomal dominant axonal CMT2CC.

genes/9.notes: Neurofilament heavy chain; 3' UTR read-through frameshift variants create a cryptic amyloidogenic element causing autosomal dominant axonal CMT2CC.

evidence.snippet: we report a novel c.423G-->T (Lys141Asn) missense mutation of small heat-shock protein 22-kDa protein 8 (encoded by HSPB8), which is also responsible for distal hereditary motor neuropathy type (dHMN) II
evidence.explanation: Establishes HSPB8 as causative for CMT2L in the pedigree that defined the locus.

genes/10.notes: Encodes the small heat-shock protein HSP22. Substitutions at Lys141 in the alpha-crystallin domain cause CMT2L and, allelically, distal hereditary motor neuropathy; mutant HSP22 is degeneration-inducing selectively in motor neurons.

evidence.snippet: Our report documents in 18 patients the deleterious impact of a mutation in human cytoplasmic AlaRS and broadens the spectrum of defects found in tRNA synthetases.
evidence.explanation: Human genetic support for AARS1 as the CMT2N gene across two founder-distinct families.

evidence.snippet: Our results showed that p.Arg329His AARS also segregated with CMT disease in a large Australian family.
evidence.explanation: Independent family replicating segregation of the recurrent AARS1 allele with CMT.

genes/11.notes: Cytoplasmic alanyl-tRNA synthetase. The recurrent p.Arg329His allele has arisen on more than one founder background and reduces tRNA(Ala) charging.

evidence.snippet: in exon 8 of dehydrogenase E1 and transketolase domain-containing 1 (DHTKD1) in all eight affected individuals
evidence.explanation: Co-segregation of the DHTKD1 nonsense allele with CMT2 in the linked pedigree.

genes/12.notes: Dehydrogenase E1 and transketolase domain-containing protein 1, part of a 2-oxoglutarate-dehydrogenase-complex-like protein. The human genetic support for CMT2Q that this entry cites is a single linked five-generation pedigree with a nonsense allele degraded by nonsense-mediated decay; biallelic DHTKD1 variants cause 2-aminoadipic and 2-oxoadipic aciduria instead.

evidence.snippet: p.Ala397Thr MARS supported very little yeast cell growth, consistent with this being a loss-of-function allele.
evidence.explanation: Yeast complementation evidence that the CMT2U MARS1 allele is loss-of-function.

genes/13.notes: Cytoplasmic methionyl-tRNA synthetase. Reported in a small number of CMT2U families; the CMT2U alleles behave as loss-of-function in yeast complementation. Biallelic MARS1 variants cause an interstitial lung and liver disease of infancy instead.

evidence.snippet: A significant 36–54% (mean 45%, P > 0.001) decrease in enzyme activity was observed for all carriers of the mutation
evidence.explanation: Quantifies the loss of alpha-N-acetylglucosaminidase activity in carriers of the p.Ile403Thr allele - a mean 45% decrease, so roughly half of normal activity is retained.

evidence.snippet: No enzymatic assay was performed on Family 2.
evidence.explanation: The authors' own statement that the second family's allele was not tested enzymatically, which is part of why no mechanism edge is asserted for NAGLU.

genes/14.notes: Lysosomal alpha-N-acetylglucosaminidase. The CMT2V claim rests on two families in the defining report: a large French-Canadian family in which the heterozygous missense allele p.Ile403Thr segregates with a late-onset painful sensory-predominant neuropathy and carriers show a mean 45% decrease in enzyme activity, and a North-American family carrying the nonsense allele p.Glu123X, in which affected members also had mild muscular weakness and diminished reflexes. Biallelic loss causes mucopolysaccharidosis IIIB instead. No enzyme assay was performed in the second family, and how a partial enzyme deficiency produces the neuropathy is not established in nerve, so no mechanism edge to axonal degeneration is asserted for this gene.

evidence.snippet: Interestingly, we identified 15 ALS5/SPG11/KIAA1840 mutations in 12 families
evidence.explanation: Twelve families with SPG11 alleles among 28 screened autosomal recessive axonal CMT pedigrees.

genes/15.notes: Encodes spatacsin. Biallelic alleles span autosomal recessive hereditary spastic paraplegia with thin corpus callosum, juvenile ALS, and the axonal CMT2X end of that spectrum; loss of spatacsin impairs clearance of lipids from lysosomes.

evidence.snippet: We show that CMT2A patients contain a loss-of-function mutation in the motor domain of the KIF1B gene.
evidence.explanation: The original human genetic claim for KIF1B at the CMT2A locus.

evidence.snippet: As there is a human asserted with a variation in this gene, "Limited" classification must be used. The classification is not disputed at this time.
evidence.explanation: ClinGen's own summary of why KIF1B-CMT2A1 is graded Limited rather than disputed, which is the basis for the UNKNOWN relationship_type here.

genes/16.notes: Kinesin family member 1B. The CMT2A locus was originally attributed to a KIF1B motor-domain loss-of-function allele, but the relationship has not been corroborated and ClinGen's Charcot-Marie-Tooth Disease Gene Curation Expert Panel classifies KIF1B-CMT2A1 as Limited. Graded UNKNOWN rather than CAUSATIVE for that reason, and deliberately not wired to a pathophysiology node: asserting a mechanism edge would commit this entry to a gene-disease relationship the cited curation does not support.

evidence.snippet: A unique homozygous mutation in LMNA (which encodes lamin A/C, a component of the nuclear envelope) was identified in all affected members and in additional patients with CMT2 from a third, unrelated family.
evidence.explanation: Establishes LMNA as causative for autosomal recessive CMT2 across three families.

genes/17.notes: Lamin A/C, a nuclear-envelope intermediate filament protein. A homozygous founder allele causes autosomal recessive axonal CMT2B1; other LMNA alleles cause muscular dystrophy, dilated cardiomyopathy and partial lipodystrophy.

evidence.snippet: We show that the patient fibroblasts are practically devoid of TRIM2, through mRNA and protein instability caused by the mutations.
evidence.explanation: Patient-fibroblast assay demonstrating that the CMT2R TRIM2 alleles leave essentially no TRIM2 protein.

genes/18.notes: E3 ubiquitin ligase whose substrates include neurofilament light chain. Biallelic loss-of-function alleles cause early-onset axonal neuropathy (CMT2R); the index report describes a single patient, with the phenotypic spectrum extended by later series.

evidence.snippet: We identified a novel VCP mutation (p.Glu185Lys) segregating in an autosomal dominant Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2 family.
evidence.explanation: The single family establishing VCP as a CMT2Y gene.

genes/19.notes: Facilitates protein degradation by the proteasomal and autophagic pathways. The CMT2Y claim rests on one autosomal dominant family whose p.Glu185Lys allele impairs autophagic flux; other VCP alleles cause inclusion body myopathy with Paget disease and frontotemporal dementia, hereditary spastic paraplegia and a minority of familial ALS.

evidence.snippet: Here, we describe five additional patients from two unrelated families with sensorimotor axonal neuropathy without hepatocerebral affection caused by homozygous MPV17 variants.
evidence.explanation: Two further unrelated families with homozygous MPV17 alleles and isolated axonal neuropathy.

genes/20.notes: Mitochondrial inner-membrane protein involved in deoxynucleotide homeostasis. Biallelic alleles cause the axonal sensorimotor neuropathy CMT2EE as well as the hepatocerebral mitochondrial DNA depletion syndrome; the neuropathy-only presentations reported so far lack liver and brain involvement.

evidence.snippet: Seven missense changes were identified that segregated within individual pedigrees
evidence.explanation: Seven segregating ATP1A1 missense alleles across the multi-country CMT2 cohort.

evidence.snippet: Five mutants fall into a remarkably narrow motif within the helical linker region that couples the nucleotide-binding and phosphorylation domains.
evidence.explanation: Source for the helical-linker clustering stated in this record's notes.

genes/21.notes: Alpha-1 subunit of the Na+,K+-ATPase, localized to the axolemma of myelinated sensory and motor axons. Five of the seven substitutions in the defining cohort fall in the helical linker coupling the nucleotide-binding and phosphorylation domains.

evidence.snippet: We examined a Korean family in which two individuals had an autosomal-dominant axonal CMT with early-onset, sensory ataxia, tremor, and slow disease progression.
evidence.explanation: Defines the extent of the human observation behind the DGAT2 claim - two affected individuals in one family.

genes/22.notes: Diacylglycerol O-acyltransferase 2, catalysing the final step of triglyceride synthesis. The whole of the human genetic support is one Korean family with two affected members and a de novo missense allele, supported by cell-proliferation and zebrafish assays. Graded UNKNOWN, and not wired to a pathophysiology node.

evidence.snippet: Six novel variants were identified by WES, but only DCAF8 p.R317C tracked with affected status within the family.
evidence.explanation: Segregation analysis identifying DCAF8 p.R317C as the only candidate tracking with disease in the family.

genes/23.notes: Substrate receptor of the Cullin-4-DDB1 E3 ubiquitin ligase. A single missense allele reported in one family weakens DCAF8-DDB1 binding and is associated with axonal neuropathy carrying infrequent giant axons with neurofilament accumulation.

evidence.snippet: Severe early-onset axonal neuropathy due to MFN2 mutations can present as an apparently recessively inherited neuropathy but the minimal phenotype in the parents suggests a semi-dominant mechanism.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the biallelic MFN2 presentation and its semi-dominant rather than fully recessive character.

evidence.snippet: All parents were asymptomatic or mildly symptomatic with some signs of peripheral neuropathy indicating a minimal phenotype.
evidence.explanation: The carrier-parent finding behind the semi-dominant reading recorded in these notes.

evidence.snippet: In summary, MFN2 is DEFINITIVELY associated with semidominant axonal hereditary motor and sensory neuropathy due to the presence of both genetic case level evidence and experimental evidence.
evidence.explanation: ClinGen's Charcot-Marie-Tooth Disease Gene Curation Expert Panel independently classifies the MFN2 neuropathy relationship as semidominant, supporting the semi-dominant reading of the biallelic presentation.

genes/24.notes: Homozygous or compound heterozygous MFN2 variants produce severe early-onset axonal neuropathy, designated CMT2A2B and separated in OMIM/MONDO from the dominant CMT2A2A. The heterozygous parents of the reported probands carried the single variants and were asymptomatic or only minimally affected, which the authors read as semi-dominant rather than strictly recessive inheritance. ClinGen's Charcot-Marie-Tooth Disease Gene Curation Expert Panel reaches the same conclusion independently, classifying MFN2 as Definitive for semidominant axonal hereditary motor and sensory neuropathy.

evidence.snippet: Mutations in the mitofusin 2 (MFN2) gene, which encodes a mitochondrial GTPase mitofusin protein, have recently been reported to cause both Charcot-Marie-Tooth 2A (CMT2A) and hereditary motor and sensory neuropathy VI (HMSN VI).
evidence.explanation: Establishes MFN2 as the causal gene for HMSN VI as well as CMT2A.

evidence.snippet: We identified two HMSN VI families with the R364W mutation in the early onset group; however, two other families with the same mutation did not have optic atrophy.
evidence.explanation: Supports the statement in these notes that optic atrophy is not allele-specific in MFN2 neuropathy.

evidence.snippet: Phenotype was variable in many studies, even with the same mutation, as some families had optic atrophy, but others did not.
evidence.explanation: ClinGen's own evidence summary records that optic atrophy varies between families carrying the same MFN2 variant, which is why HMSN VIA is curated as an MFN2 subtype rather than a separate disease.

evidence.snippet: In addition, two early onset families with R94W mutations, previously reported for HMSN VI, did not have visual impairment.
evidence.explanation: The second discordant observation behind the statement that optic atrophy is not allele-specific, in families whose variant had been reported as HMSN VI.

genes/25.notes: MFN2 is the gene behind hereditary motor and sensory neuropathy type VI, axonal CMT accompanied by optic atrophy. Optic atrophy is not allele-specific: in a 62-family screen two R364W families had optic atrophy and two others with the same variant did not, and two early-onset R94W families previously reported as HMSN VI had no visual impairment. This record is kept separate from the dominant CMT2A record only so that the OMIM/MONDO HMSN6A concept has a reciprocal gene assertion; the gene and its mechanism are the same.

evidence.snippet: We have identified-by whole exome sequencing-three unrelated families, including one de novo patient, with axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease (CMT2) sharing the same private variant in CADM3, Tyr172Cys.
evidence.explanation: Establishes CADM3 Tyr172Cys as the causal variant in three unrelated CMT2 families.

evidence.snippet: Most CADM3 patients share a similar phenotype consisting of autosomal dominant CMT2 with marked upper limb involvement.
evidence.explanation: Sources the autosomal dominant inheritance and upper-limb-predominant phenotype recorded here.

genes/26.notes: A single recurrent CADM3 variant, Tyr172Cys, was found in three unrelated families including one de novo case, and is absent from 230,000 control chromosomes in gnomAD. CADM3 is the axonal member of the CADM adhesion pair that organizes the myelinated fibre with Schwann-cell CADM4. Inheritance is autosomal dominant. A search of the approved symbol CADM3 in the ClinGen Gene-Disease Validity CSV (snapshot 2026-08-13) returns no row, so no expert panel has yet classified this relationship.
